obligation: Internal report of a suspected incident (all incidents; CJI rule applied company-wide)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6a (binding through the CJIS Security Addendum sec. 3.01; 28 CFR 20.33(a)(7)); POL-03 4.2
trigger: Any workforce member suspects an incident, including one found in an agency-hosted system
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Incident line or the Security Operations Manager (incident commander)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - AG-02 and AG-39 contracts incorporate the Security Addendum; POL-03 applies the same rule to all incidents

obligation: Company notice to AG-02 and AG-39 of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; AG-02 and AG-39 contracts; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve CJI or CHRI, in the ACMC or in AG-02 systems the company administers
deadline: IR-6b sets no separate deadline. Contracts and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery, without waiting for the company's investigation
notify: AG-02 local agency security officer and AG-39 terminal agency coordinator, who route the report to the CJIS Systems Officer (CSO), SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and the FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Agency report of a security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty the company supports)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: Addendum sets no deadline; follows each state CSA's procedure (Florida for AG-02; State B for AG-39, to be mapped)
notify: The agency reports to its CSO and the Director, FBI, with the actions taken by the agency and the company. The FBI may suspend access and require CHRI to be deleted or returned
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company supplies its actions and evidence on request

obligation: Company notice to AG-01 of a possible FTI disclosure or unauthorized inspection
citation: N92-R01: Pub. 1075 Exhibit 7 (AG-01 contract); Pub. 1075 sec. 1.8.2; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, including a breach or incident in the FTI enclave, its backups, logs, or interface, or FTI found outside the enclave
deadline: Immediately. Company target: within 1 hour of discovery, so AG-01 has most of its 24-hour window
notify: AG-01 disclosure officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards report of an FTI incident, data breach, or unauthorized inspection
trigger: Discovery of a possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, or a data breach. Do not wait for an internal investigation to confirm FTI was involved
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery
notify: TIGTA Field Division Special Agent-in-Charge and the IRS Office of Safeguards (data incident report without FTI in it)
applies_at_this_tier: AG-01 files. Sec. 1.8.2 also places the duty on any person who discovers a possible improper disclosure, so the company confirms with AG-01 within the 24 hours that the report was made and reports directly if it cannot confirm

obligation: Taxpayer notice after unauthorized FTI access (agency duty)
trigger: The agency proposes disciplinary or adverse action against the employee responsible for an unauthorized inspection or disclosure
deadline: Written notice to the taxpayer; the agency confirms completion to the Office of Safeguards and shares any draft media release before distribution
notify: Affected taxpayers; IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: AG-01 decides. For a company employee (insider runbook), AG-01 and counsel decide how this applies; the media-release step applies in both runbooks

obligation: Florida state agency ransomware report (AG-01, AG-03, other state agencies)
trigger: Ransomware incident at a state agency, including one in a contractor-hosted system the agency uses
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and the Cybercrime Office of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company notifies each state agency within 1 hour and supplies the required content (facts, most recent backup and whether affected, data types, fiscal impact, ransom details)

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report (AG-02, AG-04 to AG-38 as applicable)
trigger: Ransomware incident affecting a county or municipality ("local government" in 282.3185(2)), including systems the company administers
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company supplies the same content. AG-02 is a sheriff's office and AG-04 a tax collector; each decides with its county whether 282.3185 reaches it, and gets the company's notice within 1 hour either way

obligation: Local government after-action report
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons learned in time

obligation: Prohibition on ransom payment by Florida agencies
trigger: Ransom demand to a state agency, county, or municipality
deadline: Applies at all times: these customers may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-03 4.7)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds the Florida state agency, county, and municipal customers. The company will not pay in a way any agency objects to

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to each affected Florida agency
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) in a system the company maintains for an agency. Access by an employee is not a breach only if it is in good faith and the information is not used for an unrelated purpose
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida agency (the covered entity). Include all information the agency needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the company as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h))

obligation: Agency notice to Florida individuals
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; law enforcement may delay
notify: Each affected Florida resident
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company may send notices on an agency's behalf if asked (501.171(6)(b)) and supplies counts by tenant and state of residence

obligation: Agency notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; the company supplies counts of Florida residents per tenant

obligation: Agency notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Breach and incident duties for State B and State C customers and for residents of other states
citation: Breach notification and agency incident reporting law of each state where the agency sits or affected individuals reside
trigger: Incident affecting AG-39 to AG-43, or individuals who live outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state (counsel maps the clocks into this matrix by 2026-11-30, POAM-012)
notify: Each agency; residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - through contracts and each state's law. Until mapped, the company gives these agencies the same 1-hour notice as Florida agencies

obligation: SNAP, TANF, and Medicaid applicant data (AG-03)
trigger: Unauthorized access to AG-03 applicant or household data
deadline: The cited rules limit use and disclosure but set no incident notice deadline for the contractor. Clocks come from the AG-03 contract (POL-03 4.4: 1 hour) and Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)
notify: AG-03 information security manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - through the AG-03 contract. AG-03 decides any reporting to its federal program agencies

obligation: Motor vehicle record information (AG-04)
trigger: Unauthorized access to, or use of, motor vehicle record personal information
deadline: The DPPA sets no notice deadline. It makes knowingly obtaining or disclosing the data for an unpermitted use unlawful (2722(a)) and gives individuals a civil action with liquidated damages of $2,500 (2724). Clocks come from the AG-04 contract (1 hour) and Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)
notify: AG-04 records custodian, who informs the state motor vehicle agency under its data-access terms
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - through the AG-04 contract

obligation: Managed services incident in an agency-hosted system
citation: Managed services contracts; POL-03 4.11; N92-R02 for AG-02 systems
trigger: Suspected incident in a server the company administers for an agency
deadline: Contract: notice within 1 hour; severity 1 response within 4 hours
notify: Agency IT contact and security officer; the agency's incident lead commands its own systems
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: SP 800-53 IR-6(3) (Moderate baseline); CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving a cloud, SaaS, or remote management service
deadline: No deadline set; as soon as practicable
notify: Cloud provider, identity provider, MDR provider, or SYS-10 vendor security incident channel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract (SP 800-53 Moderate)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment. Full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
citation: OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) mitigating factor; company practice
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed; for insider cases, when counsel advises
deadline: Company target: within 48 hours of declaration (ransomware)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Coordinate with the agencies, which report to FDLE under Florida law

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Board and private equity sponsor notice
trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Same day
notify: Audit committee chair; sponsor operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - governance, not legal

obligation: HIPAA breach notification
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Not applicable
notify: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - no customer has designated the company a business associate; AG-03 placed its eligibility functions outside its health care component (45 CFR 164.105)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. The proposed size criterion could reach the company if it is treated as critical infrastructure; recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held

obligation: Covered telecommunications and Kaspersky reports
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article, identified under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
